title: Pocketwire Pay in 4 Terms: One Account per Customer
content:
## Pocketwire Pay in 4 Terms — Number of Accounts per Customer

**1.** A customer may hold one Pocketwire Pay in 4 account. The limit is 1 account per customer.

**2.** An account is opened only if the customer holds no other Pay in 4 account whose status is anything other than closed.

**3.** Whether another account stands in the way is read from the company's own records of the customer's Pocketwire Pay in 4 accounts and the status each one shows at the time of the application, not from the customer's description of them. The accounts compared are those recorded under the same customer.

### Status of an existing account and its effect on a new application

A Pocketwire Pay in 4 account passes through the statuses applied, active, past due, suspended and closed.

| Status of the customer's existing Pocketwire Pay in 4 account | Does it stand in the way of opening another account? |
|---|---|
| applied | Yes |
| active | Yes |
| past due | Yes |
| suspended | Yes |
| closed | No |
| no existing account | No |

Where the customer holds several earlier accounts, a single one in a status other than closed is enough to stand in the way; accounts that are all closed do not.

### Basis Q&A

**Does a closed account count toward the limit of one?**
No. Clause 2 looks only at accounts whose status is anything other than closed, so an account that has been closed — whether it was declined at the eligibility check or closed later — does not prevent a new account from being opened under this clause.

**Does an account that is still at the application stage count?**
Yes. An account in the applied status is not closed, so while it exists no second Pocketwire Pay in 4 account is opened.

**Does this clause alone decide that a new account will be opened?**
No. It sets only the one-account limit; an application that clears it is still subject to the other conditions of Pocketwire Pay in 4 account opening.
